StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is exactly what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). StackType's only non-presentation readers are GetTypeForAmount (PowerModel.cs:462) and InvokePowerModified's VFX split (Creature.cs:628). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

ShouldScaleInMultiplayer.rationale: Multiplayer-only. ShouldScaleInMultiplayer / GetScaledAmountForMultiplayer feed PowerCmd.Apply's MultiplayerScalingModel leg (PowerCmd.cs:128-131), already waived as step 14 of audit/records/seam/power_cmd.json. The sim is single-player.

AfterSideTurnEnd.issue: Both legs are in the wrong slot and the IsDead guard is missing. RegenPower.cs:20-28 is `if (participants.Contains(Owner) && !Owner.IsDead) { Heal(Amount); Decrement; }` on AfterSideTurnEnd. (a) The ENEMY leg uses the per-creature on_enemy_turn_end (powers.py:165-167) instead of the side-scoped on_enemy_side_end -- see the dedicated guard entry. (b) The PLAYER leg uses on_player_turn_end (powers.py:169-171), which is Hook.BeforeTurnEnd (combat.py:654), one slot before the sim's real AfterTurnEnd equivalent after_player_turn_end (combat.py:665); the game heals AFTER the turn-end card effects and the hand flush, the sim before them. (c) `!Owner.IsDead` is absent from _apply_regen (powers.py:160-163): CreatureCmd.heal does return 0 for a dead target (cmds.py:160-161) so no HP moves, but `self._tick()` still runs and still fires on_power_amount_changed, so a dead-but-retained owner burns a Regen stack the game would keep. ALL DORMANT, for one shared reason: the only ported Regen source in the sim is a potion (potions.py:613), and potions are out of scope by the shared contract's global-scope rule, so no in-scope content puts Regen on anybody. Named trigger: any non-potion Regen source -- at which point (b) becomes live immediately (the heal races the flush) and (a) becomes live with two or more enemies. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.issue: Same mechanism as turn_structure gap G5 (the enemy side is per-enemy in the sim, per-side in the game): the sim's on_enemy_turn_end (combat.py:341) runs immediately after THIS enemy's move, where Hook.AfterTurnEnd -- the dispatcher for AbstractModel.AfterSideTurnEnd (Hook.cs:1267-1292) -- runs once at CombatManager.cs:1256 after EVERY enemy has moved. The sim does have the right slot available: on_enemy_side_end (combat.py:345). Per binding rule 3 the mechanism keeps G5's `gap` verdict and is cross-referenced rather than re-argued. Reproduce the affected population with `py audit/tools/power_census.py slots`. Third-file citations, not hashed here.
Absent from the sim -- see clause (c) of the AfterSideTurnEnd entry. Carried as its own guard because it is a distinct omission from the slot problem and would survive a slot fix.

guards.rationale: powers.py:163 `self._tick()` decrements by 1 and expires at <= 0 (powers.py:70-75), which is Decrement plus ShouldRemoveDueToAmount for a non-AllowNegative power. Note the ORDER matches too: C# heals first and decrements second, so the heal uses the pre-decrement Amount, and powers.py:162-163 does the same.
